Ct. No. 237 Pradipta Das Sarma vs State Of West Bengal & Anr
on 9 December, 2024

Saikat
 Ct. No. 237 Pradipta Das Sarma
 Vs.
 State of West Bengal & Anr.
 Mr. Shataroop Purkayastha, Adv.
 Ms. Jagriti Bhattacharya, Adv.
 ...For the Petitioner.
 Mr. Joydeep Roy, Jr. Govt. Adv.
 Ms. Rita Dutta, Adv.
 ...For the State.

This is an application where petitioner has prayed for quashing of the G.R. Case No.4898 of 2016,
presently pending before learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Barrackpore.

It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the marriage between the present petitioner and the opposite party No.2 was solemnised on 31st July, 2014 at Chinsurah, Hooghly and the ceremony of boubhat was organised on 3rd August, 2014.

On the next date the present petitioner had been to Chinsurah with the opposite party No.2 who took some photographs of the petitioner and threatened him implicating in false cases alleging, inter alia, that the petitioner married severally and that he had inflicted torture upon opposite party No.2.
Learned advocate for the petitioner further submits that the marriage was not even consummated.

However, opposite party No.2 herein lodged a written complaint before the Inspector-in-Charge,
Belgharia Police Station on 21st July, 2016 alleging, inter alia, that she was tortured on the demand of dowry by her in-laws.
After completion of investigation police submitted charge-sheet against the petitioner under section 498/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

He further submits that from the charge-sheet it transpires that investigating officer did not state anything about guilt of present petitioner and also it appears from the charge-sheet that no such incident took place, as alleged by the opposite party No.2 herein.
Being aggrieved by the impugned proceeding, the petitioner herein contended that learned Magistrate in the court below while taking cognizance failed to appreciate that in the charge-sheet there is no mention of any date when the incident allegedly had taken place.

Learned court below failed to appreciate that the complainant did not lead conjugal life with the petitioner and as such Ct. No. 237 Pradipta Das Sarma vs State Of West Bengal & Anr on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166793241/

sentences.text: The opposite party No.2 admitted that she did not reside at her in-laws' house but failed to explain as such how she was threatened by the petitioner.
Accordingly, the allegation that the opposite party No.2 was driven out from her matrimonial house on 13th July, 2015 is baseless and no cogent evidence was produced by her.
Accordingly, the petitioner has prayed for quashing of entire proceeding.
Opposite party No.2, de facto complainant is not represented.
Learned counsel on behalf of the State placed the Case Diary and based his arguments on three statements recorded by the investigating officer during investigation.
He submits that there is no incriminating material against any particular accused in the Case Diary.

Supreme Court on numerous occasion have expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A of I.P.C and the vindictiveness in implicating husband and his relatives in family dispute over breakdown of marriage, without considering it's long term ramifications of a faade Trial before a Criminal court.

Coming to the facts of the present case it appears from the contents of complaint as well as three statements recorded during investigation that general allegations are leveled against the accused persons including present petitioner the complainant alleged that "sasur bari lokera" ( men of matrimonial house) had inflicted torture upon her.
No Specific and distinct allegations have been made against any of the accused including petitioner herein.

In Neelu Chopra & another Vs. Bharti, (2009) 10 SCC 184, Apex Court specifically held what is required to brought to the notice of the court in lodging a proper complaint paragraph 9 & 10 runs as follow:-
"9.

entities.text: Neelu Chopra & another Vs. Bharti, (2009) 10 SCC 184
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to lodge a proper complaint, mere mention of the sections and the language of those sections is not the be all and end all of the matter.

What is required to be brought to the notice of the court is the particulars of the offence committed by each and every accused and the role played by each and every accused in committing of that offence.
10. When we see the complaint, the complaint is sadly vague.
It does not show as to which accused has committed what offence and what is the exact role played by these appellants in the commission of offence.
There could be said something against Rajesh, as the allegations are made against him more precisely but he is no more and has already expired.

Under such circumstances, it would be an abuse of the process of law to allow the prosecution to continue against the aged parents of Rajesh, the present appellants herein, on the basis of a vague and general complaint which is silent about the precise acts of the appellants."

Therefore on perusal of FIR, the final report and all other documents accompanying it, I am satisfied that no case is made out against the petitioner and the pendency of the proceeding against him is an abuse of process of court.
